## What does it mean to say a package supports AD?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
- A real model needs a PPL, and a PPL needs gradients through every
  component
- Nobody has written down what supporting AD means, so we picked a
  definition and made CI defend it
- `DifferentiationInterfaceTest` does the correctness testing and the
  benchmarks. One list drives the CI matrix, the Codecov flags and the
  README badges. Seven configurations in the list, six in every package

::: {.callout-note}
Is there a guide for any of this anywhere in the Julia ecosystem? I went
looking and did not find one.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
```julia
const _AD_BACKENDS = [
  (header = "ForwardDiff", ...),
  (header = "ReverseDiff (tape)", ...),
  (header = "ReverseDiff (compiled)", ...),
  (header = "Enzyme forward", ...),
  (header = "Enzyme reverse", ...),
  (header = "Mooncake reverse", ...),
  (header = "Mooncake forward", ...),
]
```

::: {.attribution}
Abridged from `_AD_BACKENDS`, `src/scaffold.jl` in
`EpiAwarePackageTools.jl` at commit `427d4f5`, read 2026-08-12. Each entry
also carries a Codecov flag, a test item tag and the package it loads ·
ReverseDiff (compiled) was added by commit `4e83318` on 2026-08-10 and is
in the `ad.yaml` caller and README of `EpiAwareADTools.jl` only, checked
across the package clones 2026-08-12 · `check_broken` and the registry
contract are in `src/ad_harness.jl` ·
[DifferentiationInterfaceTest.jl](https://github.com/JuliaDiff/DifferentiationInterface.jl).
:::
:::
::::

## A wrong number, not an error

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
```julia
f(x) = xlogy(x[1], 0.8)   # d/dx = log(0.8)

DI.gradient(f, DI.AutoForwardDiff(), [0.0])
DI.gradient(f, DI.AutoMooncake(), [0.0])
```

| Backend | Gradient at `x = 0` |
|---|---|
| Finite differences | -0.22314 |
| ForwardDiff | -0.22314 |
| ReverseDiff | -0.22314 |
| Enzyme | -0.22314 |
| Mooncake | **0.0** |
:::
::: {.column width="52%"}
- `logpdf(Gamma(k, θ), x)` computes `xlogy(k - 1, x / θ)`. Mooncake has
  no rule for `xlogy`, so it differentiates the implementation. At shape
  1.0 the first argument is zero, the `iszero` branch returns a
  constant, and the gradient comes back as zero
- Nothing throws. The sampler runs. The number is wrong
- `EpiAwareADTools.jl` carries the rule, and deletes it the day
  Mooncake ships one

::: {.attribution}
The three lines and the backend comparison are from
[ComposedDistributions.jl#99][cd99], 2026-07-07. `xlogy` comes from
`LogExpFunctions`, `DI` is `DifferentiationInterface`. Mooncake 0.5.37,
Julia 1.12 · the withdrawn upstream report is
[chalk-lab/Mooncake.jl#1241][mc1241], closed the day it was opened, and
nothing has replaced it as of 2026-08-11 · the local rule is
`ext/EpiAwareADToolsLogExpFunctionsMooncakeExt.jl`.
:::
:::
::::

[cd99]: https://github.com/EpiAware/ComposedDistributions.jl/issues/99
[mc1241]: https://github.com/chalk-lab/Mooncake.jl/issues/1241
